notable_absence.finding: The total_queries_validation_error field states 'when the query request included a validate property in the ctl object' and links to 'https://docs.couchbase.com/server/8.0/search/search-request-params.html#validate' - naming a 'validate' property of the ctl object that round 22's own search-request-params.json extraction (search:ctl-object's origin record) does not mention anywhere in its concepts, relations, or notable_absence. Either that property was present on the page but not captured in round 22, or it lives at a separate anchor round 22's read did not surface in detail - left as a finding for reconciliation rather than guessed at, since this page alone is not authoritative for search-request-params.md's content.

cross_component_finding: This page's Cluster/Index Statistics field tables repeatedly state the exact Web-Console-dashboard chart name for a REST field, in the form 'This statistic appears on the Server Web Console dashboard as **X**' - directly confirming, with the literal underlying field name, several of the 18 chart names round 23's fts-monitor.md record deliberately left unminted as separate concepts. Verbatim pairs found on this page: avg_queries_latency = 'Search Query Latency', doc_count = 'Search Docs', num_bytes_used_disk = 'Search Disk Size', num_files_on_disk = 'Search Disk Files', num_root_memorysegments = 'Search Memory Segments', num_root_filesegments = 'Search Disk Segments', num_mutations_to_index = 'Search Mutations Remaining', num_pindexes_actual = 'Search Partitions', num_pindexes_target = 'Search Partitions Expected', num_recs_to_persist = 'Search Records to Persist', total_bytes_indexed = 'Search Index Rate', total_bytes_query_results = 'Search Result Rate', total_compaction_written_bytes = 'Search Compaction Rate', total_queries_error = 'Search Query Error Rate', total_queries_slow = 'Search Slow Queries', total_queries_timeout = 'Search Query Timeout Rate', total_term_searchers = 'Term Searchers Start Rate'. No relation was forced between fts:search-index-statistics and fts:nsstats-endpoint for this, since one is a UI-chart family and the other a REST field family - different shapes - but this is exactly the kind of same-underlying-metric-two-names finding round 23's own notable_absence anticipated a future round might supply.
